prediction.likelyOutcome: Lagoon should recover most or all of the $364,212 in unpaid rent essentially as a matter of law, but the far larger accelerated/future-rent component is likely to survive summary judgment only in part (or be continued for further discovery) given the genuine, well-evidenced dispute over Lagoon's redevelopment of the property and its effect on mitigation and the liquidated-damages calculation. Net recovery is likely to land well below the full $1,808,470 demanded, with the future-rent piece the main variable pending Abdul's deposition and completion of discovery.

issues.label: Accelerated Future Rent Under Liquidated-Damages Clause
Procedural Prematurity of Summary Judgment Motion

outcome.description: The district court granted Lagoon summary judgment in June 2022, held the liquidated-damages clause enforceable so that no mitigation was required, and (after Lagoon waived attorney fees) entered judgment for $1,808,470 plus costs. The Minnesota Court of Appeals reversed on December 11, 2023, holding the liquidated-damages clause unenforceable because actual damages were capable of estimation and the clause ignored the duty to mitigate, and remanded for further proceedings on actual damages and mitigation.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed (liquidated-damages clause unenforceable) and remanded; no final figure yet.
